blocks.content: To protect the interest of and secure fair treatment to policyholders.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Protecting the interests of policyholders and ensuring fair treatment in all insurance transactions.
Promoting speedy and orderly growth of the insurance industry for the benefit of the common man.
Ensuring financial soundness, integrity, and high standards of competence among market players.
Ensuring speedy settlement of genuine claims and preventing insurance frauds and malpractices.
Setting up effective grievance redressal machinery to resolve policyholder complaints.

rows: Open competitive market with public and private insurers
Direct control by the Ministry of Finance
Limited formal channels for grievance redressal
Dedicated Ombudsman machinery and IGMS mechanism

items: IRDAI was established following the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee (1993-94).
Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 specifies the duties, powers, and functions of the Authority.
IRDAI regulates both insurance companies (Life, General, Health) and insurance intermediaries (Agents, Brokers, TPA).
